reference_aircraft: Cessna 172S Skyhawk SP (Lycoming IO-360-L2A, 180 hp, fixed-pitch propeller), normal category
description: Four-seat high-wing trainer. Simulation reference: Cessna 172S. Public name, branding and artwork are fictional; only public specifications and published performance are used. Structural frame: origin at the front face of the firewall (the C172 datum) on the thrust line; X forward, Y right, Z down (m).

sources.citation: Cessna Model 172S Pilot's Operating Handbook and FAA Approved Airplane Flight Manual, Revision 5 (2004): sections 1 (dimensions, weights, capacities), 2 (limitations), 5 (performance), 6 (weight and balance).
FAA Type Certificate Data Sheet 3A12 (Cessna 172 series): control surface movements, datum, CG range.
Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections (1959): NACA 2412, NACA 0012 section data.
USAF Stability and Control DATCOM (1978): lift-curve slope, downwash, flap effectiveness methods.
Roskam, Airplane Design Part V/VI: radius-of-gyration method for inertia estimates; component drag build-up.
Engineering estimate by the Aviation Dynamics project; see docs/aircraft/tupi-t180.md.

provenance.note: Standard empty weight 1663 lb (incl. unusable fuel and full oil).
Auxiliary fuel pump current ~4 A (5 A breaker), drawn only while the pump switch is on.

Battery model: loaded plateau 24.4 V charged / 23.0 V at 2 % with a surface charge of up to +1.1 V built by the alternator in ~1 min and stripped by a load in ~40 s; charge acceptance tapers to ~2 A at full (ammeter settles near +2 A in cruise, as a 172S does).
Typical delivered C172S empty CG ~39.6 in aft of datum; height estimated.
Chosen so the gross-weight totals fall near the commonly quoted C172 values (Ixx~1285, Iyy~1825, Izz~2667 kg m^2); no manufacturer source.
2550 lb normal category.
Maximum ramp weight 2558 lb, normal category, in the POH revision that gives 2550 lb take-off (EASA TCDS: later revisions without kit MK172-72-01 give 2457 lb ramp / 2450 lb take-off).
Standard empty weight includes unusable fuel (3 gal) and full oil; the tanks hold the unusable fuel, so it is not counted twice.
Baggage area 1 (sta. 82-108) 120 lb, area 2 (sta. 108-142) 50 lb; maximum combined weight for areas 1 and 2 is 120 lb.
Arms: front seats 37 in, rear seats 73 in, baggage A 95 in, baggage B 123 in.
35.0 in at 1950 lb and below, 41.0 in at 2550 lb (normal category).
47.3 in at all weights (normal category).
Wing area 174 sq ft, span 36 ft 1 in, MAC ~58.8 in.
Two-panel planform (constant-chord inboard, tapered outboard) matching span and area; incidence +1.5 root / -1.5 tip, dihedral 1.73 deg.

NACA 2412 2-D slope, zero-lift angle and smooth-section cl_max 1.60 at Re ~3e6 (Abbott & von Doenhoff); with the lifting line the clean stall speed follows without calibration. Flap dclmax/dcl (0.55) calibrated to the flaps-30 stall.
Aileron 20 up / 15 down; flaps 0-30 deg. Flap effectiveness and drag: calibrated/estimated.

Horizontal tail span 11 ft 4 in (POH), area/chords estimated; elevator 28 up / 23 down (TCDS); incidence and slipstream exposure calibrated so the elevator is near neutral in cruise and the nose wheel lifts near 50 KIAS on the take-off roll.
Vertical tail geometry estimated; rudder travel 17.7 deg each way (TCDS 17 deg 44 min).

Component drag areas from a Roskam-style build-up, scaled to match POH cruise (124 KTAS at 75% power, 8000 ft) and max speed (126 KTAS at sea level). The gear and strut body shapes (axis, length, thickness) are estimated from the 3-D model and only drive the airflow view's wakes.
Lycoming IO-360-L2A, 180 bhp at 2700 rpm, 361 cu in.

Mechanical friction (rubbing, accessories) mep, quadratic in speed; the pumping loop (ambient minus manifold pressure) is modelled separately. 130 kPa at 2,700 rpm so that friction plus the full-throttle pumping loss is 13.2 % of rated power there, which is what the Lycoming sea-level/altitude curve and Gagg-Farrar (P/P0 = 1.132 sigma - 0.132) imply (with the charge heating the ISA lapse sits 1-4 % below that line above 4,000 ft); shape after Heywood.
IO-360-L2A, 8.5:1 (Lycoming type certificate data); sets the residual-gas loss of volumetric efficiency at low manifold pressure, eta_v ~ (r_c - p_exhaust/p_intake)/(r_c - 1).

0.89 at full throttle, rated rpm, referred to manifold density: the value implied by the published full-rich take-off fuel flow (about 16 gph, 96 lb/h, at an equivalence ratio of 1.25-1.3), which with the rated power fixes the indicated efficiency (0.33) and so the fuel flows at every power.

Inlet-port flow loss growing as speed squared (Heywood 6.2.4): 0.08 reproduces the rise of full-throttle torque below rated rpm in the Lycoming sea-level curve (about 180/166/155/143/131 hp at 2,700/2,400/2,200/2,000/1,800 rpm, transcribed from memory; confirm against the operator's manual). It sets the power at the fixed-pitch climb rpm (about 2,250).

The idle orifice (closed plate plus idle air) is sized so MAP = 0.29 x ambient at 650 rpm; with the idle mixture full rich the engine then idles at about 700 rpm on the ground at 8.3 inHg (the idle stop a mechanic sets to 600-700 rpm). Closed, the orifice is choked, so the air flow is fixed and MAP falls as 1/rpm when the propeller windmills the engine (about 6 inHg at 1,200 rpm): the engine then absorbs power instead of producing it.
Wide-open throttle bore sized for a 3 % (0.9 inHg) drop at rated rpm; the drop scales with the square of the air flow at other speeds.

Heating of the inducted charge in the induction tract (the IO-360's heated sump), port and valve (Heywood 6.2.3): 30 K at sea-level ISA from an effective wall temperature of 420 K, growing as the air gets colder, so the air flow at a pressure altitude goes as T^-0.7 instead of the ideal gas's 1/T (Lycoming's operator's-manual correction and SAE J1349 use T^-0.5). The 30 K is calibrated to the temperature columns of the POH's maximum-rate-of-climb table (Figure 5-6, -20/0/20/40 degC): the handbook loses 60 fpm per 20 degC at 8,000 and 12,000 ft; the ideal-gas charge lost 84, the sqrt rule 42, 30 K gives 56-60 at every altitude. The volumetric efficiency stays referred to sea-level ISA, so nothing at sea level moves; the ISA full-throttle lapse sits 1-3 % below Gagg-Farrar at 4,000-12,000 ft (73 % at 8,000 ft against the handbook's chart-derived 75 %).

McCauley fixed pitch, 76 in diameter, 60 in geometric pitch (published; pitch_m 1.524). Chord distribution scaled (x1.15 from the earlier estimate) to the POH full-throttle static rpm with the swirl and compressibility BEM; section and thickness estimated. Checked against maximum speed and its rpm.
t/c typical of forged aluminium fixed-pitch blades (round shank to ~6% tip); drives the tip compressibility drag rise (tips reach M 0.7-0.8).
Two 28 gal wing tanks, 26.5 gal usable each, arm 48 in; selector LEFT/BOTH/RIGHT plus shutoff valve.
Reservoir + lines; sets the delay between tank exhaustion and engine stoppage.
24 V 12.75 Ah battery, 28 V 60 A alternator. Loads estimated.
Track 8 ft 4 in and wheelbase ~65 in (POH); stiffness/damping estimated for ~6 cm static deflection; nose steering +-10 deg (POH).
Tire inflation (POH section 8): nose 45 psi, main wheels 38 psi. Wet-runway friction and the hydroplaning speed (9 sqrt(p) kt: ~55 kt on the mains) follow from it.

0.04: middle of the 0.03-0.05 range textbooks give for dry concrete/asphalt with brakes off (Raymer, Aircraft Design, ground friction table); 0.02 is an icy-runway value. Small low-pressure GA tyres sit in the upper part of the range.

Static loads at MTOW from the geometry (nose 25 %, 2.87 kN; mains 37 % each, 4.22 kN). The cornering stiffness is the value at that load; with load it follows the usual tyre load sensitivity C_alpha = c1 N (1 - c2 N / N_ref) (Pacejka, Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics, the pKy1/pKy2 form), c2 = 0.25 so the stiffness peaks at twice the static load; a wheel unloaded by braking or a turn loses grip faster than its load.

Spin inertia of wheel and tyre: 6.00-6 main (~7 kg) 0.18 kg m^2, 5.00-5 nose (~4 kg) 0.08 kg m^2, as rings at 0.6 r^2. Sets the touchdown spin-up (~0.1 s at 50 kt) and the lock-up time under the brakes.

Brake torque capacity 350 N.m per main (Cleveland-class single-disc brakes on a 6.00-6 wheel): a full-pedal stop of about 0.3 g on a dry runway, typical of light-aircraft disc brakes; with the modelled pilot technique (1 s delay, 1 s ramp, 50 % pedal) the POH maximum-braking ground roll of 575 ft comes out within a few percent. Sliding friction 0.75 of peak (Pacejka-class tyre data). Estimated; confirm against the brake assembly rating.

POH section 7: the nose wheel is steered +-10 deg by the rudder pedals through spring-loaded steering bungees and castors to 30 deg either side under differential braking (published ranges). Modelled as a swivelling wheel with 8 cm of trail, the linkage a 2000 N m/rad spring that yields at 100 N m (half the tyre's aligning moment at its static load on dry pavement): estimated so the pedals hold the wheel within a degree at taxi speed while a brake turn swings it to the velocity.
Shape fitted to the POH airspeed calibration table (flaps up: 50 KIAS = 56 KCAS ... 140 KIAS = 138 KCAS).
Ground-adjustable rudder tab (exists on the C172): set for zero yaw moment at 105 KIAS cruise, 1500 m; aileron rigging likewise for zero roll moment.
Section 2 airspeed indicator markings: white 40-85, green 48-129, yellow 129-163, red line 163 KIAS. Verify against the POH revision of the target airplane.

Section 2 powerplant instrument markings (tach 2100-2700 green, 2700 red; oil pressure 50-90 green, 20/115 red; oil temperature 100-245 F; suction 4.5-5.5 inHg). Verify against the target POH revision.
Section 7 annunciator panel: OIL PRESS < 20 psi, LOW VAC < 3.0 inHg, VOLTS < 24.5 V, L/R LOW FUEL < ~5 gal per tank. Verify against the target POH revision.
Typical vacuum attitude gyro: ~6 deg/min erection, 70 deg pitch / 110 deg bank tumble limits, minutes to spin up/down (FAA-H-8083-15B ch. 5). Instrument-model specific; configurable.
Typical DG: mechanical drift a few deg/h, 55 deg gimbal limit (older units), re-sync every 15 min practice (FAA-H-8083-25B ch. 8).

Typical open pitot tube reads within ~1% up to 15-20 deg flow angle (NACA TN 2331 family of results); beyond it total pressure falls off. Needle natural frequency and damping are instrument estimates.
Kollsman window range 28.10-31.00 inHg is the common range of sensitive altimeters (FAA-H-8083-25B ch. 8); not airplane-specific.
Capillary time constant ~3 s gives the 6-9 s lag described in FAA-H-8083-25B ch. 8; 2000 fpm dial typical of C172 VSIs.

Electric rate gyro canted ~30 deg (FAA-H-8083-25B ch. 8). The standard-rate mark position and the bank used for calibration are instrument design estimates; the indicator responds to yaw and roll rate as the real one does.
Tube arc limit estimated from typical instrument geometry.

Card tilt limit ~18 deg typical of panel wet compasses (FAA-H-8083-25B ch. 8). Residual airframe field after compensation (hard_iron_body, fraction of the local field) chosen for a typical few-degree deviation card; each real airplane has its own, found by a compass swing. Field declination/inclination come from the world (scenarios/airports.cpp), not the aircraft.
Recovery factor ~0.8 and ~10 s time constant typical of an unshielded probe through the windshield.

Heated pitot tube (~12 mm): frontal area, droplet collection efficiency of a small cylinder (~0.8 at 50 m/s, Langmuir-Blodgett class), ice to close the inlet (~3 mm over the tip). Heater 140 W = the pitot_heat load (5 A at 28 V); half reaches the ice. Icing needs a cloud layer with liquid water in the weather.
Baseline single NAV/COM with VOR/LOC/GS indicator and transponder with encoder; GPS, ADF, DME and autopilot were options and are not installed in this profile.
Load currents are estimates for a 28 V system; switch set and breakers follow the POH electrical system description.

No bus controller: after an alternator failure the POH has the pilot shed non-essential equipment by hand (cockpit control electrical.load_shed). Kept through a shed: turn coordinator, engine and fuel gauges, fuel pump, pitot heat; the radios and lights drop (instrument lighting is non-essential).
VNE 163, VNO 129, VA 105 (2550 lb), VFE 110 (flaps 10), 85 (flaps > 10); +3.8/-1.52 g flaps up, +3.0 g flaps down.
